It applies the stock-reservation rule, where one unavailable item clears the whole reservation and throws a domain error. It also exposes queries for reserved items. The stock lookup comes in as a callback (checkStock), so the file never touches a database, an HTTP client or a framework API. It throws only domain error types and imports only domain modules. The one borderline point is the private in-memory Map of reservations keyed by orderId. That makes the service stateful and a little like a repository. But it uses no storage technology and keeps nothing beyond the process, so it reads as domain state for reservation tracking, not persistence infrastructure. I found nothing that belongs to the application, infrastructure or presentation layers. Confidence is moderate because a stricter reviewer could count that in-process reservation store as a repository-like job.
